### Project Overview
This dashboard explores the correlation between different inputs and the yield of different varieties of lettuce and tomatoes grown in a greenhouse.
20 columns with environmental conditions, management practices, and final yields.
4 crops: Tomato (40%), Cucumber (30%), Lettuce (20%), and Pepper (10%).
10,000+ rows of data.
Target : model input conditions with yield data

```{python}
# Data cleaning
# Dropping redundant columns, null values
# Describing the shape of the data
import pandas as pd
df_raw = pd.read_csv("greenhouse_crop_yields.csv")
df_clean = df_raw.dropna()

df = df_clean.copy()
df = df.drop(columns=['greenhouse_id', 'planting_date', 'harvest_date', 'days_to_maturity'])

# df_info = df.info()
# df_describe = df.describe()
```

# Lettuce analysis
```{python}
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df_lettuce_full = df[
    (df["crop_type"] == "Lettuce")
]
```
## Screening for correlation
### Row {height=70%}
```{python}
correlation_matrix = df_lettuce_full.corr(numeric_only=True)
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 10))
sns.heatmap(correlation_matrix, annot=True, fmt='.2f', cmap='coolwarm', center=0, annot_kws={'size': 7}, cbar_kws={'shrink': 0.8})
plt.title("Correlation Matrix - All Lettuce Varieties", fontsize=14)
plt.xticks(fontsize=8, rotation=45, ha='right')
plt.yticks(fontsize=8)
plt.tight_layout();
```
## Modelling positive inputs
### Row {height=70%}
```{python}
# ensure reasonable data (import all rows in contracted df_lettuce )
# there is no null value (or maybe dropna already did that)

# Column reduction based on the variables of interest depicted in the correlation analysis
df_lettuce_lite = df_lettuce_full[['crop_type', 'variety', 'light_intensity_lux', 'photoperiod_hours', 'fertilizer_N_kg_ha', 'yield_kg_per_m2']]
#line chart
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Creates 3 separate panels with different colors per variety
g = sns.lmplot(data=df_lettuce_lite, x="light_intensity_lux", y="yield_kg_per_m2", col="variety", hue="variety", col_wrap=2, height=4, aspect=1.2, legend=False)
g.fig.suptitle("Light Intensity vs Yield by Variety", y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout();

```

g.fig.suptitle("Fertilizer N vs Yield by Variety", y=1.02)

# Tomato Fertilizer Input Analysis
## Row
### 1. Total Fertilizer Data Table

```{python}
#| label: tomato_data_loading
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

df_raw = pd.read_csv("greenhouse_crop_yields.csv")
df_clean = df_raw.dropna()
df = df_clean.copy()

df["avg_temperature_C"] = (df["max_temperature_C"] + df["min_temperature_C"]) / 2
df_tomato = df[df["crop_type"] == "Tomato"].copy()

df_tomato["total_fertilizer_kg_ha"] = df_tomato["fertilizer_N_kg_ha"] + df_tomato["fertilizer_P_kg_ha"] + df_tomato["fertilizer_K_kg_ha"]

df_tomato[["variety", "fertilizer_N_kg_ha", "fertilizer_P_kg_ha", "fertilizer_K_kg_ha", "total_fertilizer_kg_ha"]].head();

```

### 2. Total Fertilizer vs Tomato Yield (Scatter Plot)

```{python}
#| label: tomato_scatter

plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4))
sns.scatterplot(data=df_tomato, x='total_fertilizer_kg_ha', y='yield_kg_per_m2', hue='variety', alpha=0.7, s=40)
plt.title('Total Fertilizer vs Tomato Yield')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show();

```

### 3. Overall Tomato Production Trendline

```{python}
#| label: tomato_trend
plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4))
sns.regplot(data=df_tomato, x='total_fertilizer_kg_ha', y='yield_kg_per_m2', scatter=False, color='red', lowess=True)
plt.title('Overall Tomato Production Trendline')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show();
```

## Physical Factor- Temperature Analysis
### 4. Temperature and Tomato Yield Statistical Table

```{python}
#| label: tomato_temp_stats
df_tomato.groupby('variety')[['avg_temperature_C', 'yield_kg_per_m2']].describe()
```

### 5. Temperature vs Tomato Yield Trend Graph

```{python}
#| label: tomato_temp_graph
sns.lmplot(data=df_tomato, x='avg_temperature_C', y='yield_kg_per_m2', hue='variety', scatter_kws={'alpha': 0.3, 's': 30}, line_kws={'linewidth': 2.5}, height=4, aspect=1.2)
plt.title('Temperature vs Tomato Yield Trend')
plt.show();
```

### 6. Tomato Yield Distribution (Swarm Plot)

```{python}
#| label: tomato_swarm
plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4))
sns.swarmplot(data=df_tomato, x='variety', y='yield_kg_per_m2', hue='variety', size=4, alpha=0.8)
plt.title('Tomato Yield Distribution (Swarm Plot)')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show();
```
